'''Petar Beron''' ([[Bulgarian language|Bulgarian]]: Петър Берон), born 14 March 1940 in [[Sofia]], [[Bulgaria]], is a Bulgarian academic and politician.<ref>{{cite book |title=Who's who in Science in Europe: A Biographical Guide in Science, Technology, Agriculture, and Medicine |volume=4 |publisher=Longman |year= 1991 |edition= 7th |page=[https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinscience0004unse_7ed/page/47/mode/2up?view=theater 47] |isbn=9780582086623 |url=https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinscience0004unse_7ed/page/n3/mode/2up |url-access=registration |via= [[Internet Archive]]}}</ref>
He was leader of the [[Union of Democratic Forces (Bulgaria)|United Democratic Forces]] (SDS) in from August 1990 to 4 December 1990 (heading the second-largest political party at the time). He was a vice-presidential candidate in [[1992 Bulgarian presidential election|1992]] and a presidential candidate in [[2001 Bulgarian presidential election|2001]] and [[2006 Bulgarian presidential election|2006]].

== Biography ==
Petar Beron was born in Sofia on 14 March 1940. He graduated from the Biology-Geology-Geography Department of the [[Sofia University|Kliment Ohridski University]] in Sofia.<ref name=Bio />

Beron is fluent in Bulgarian, Russian, English and French.<ref name=Bio />

== Academic career ==
From 1963 up to 1969 he worked as a biologist at the Institute of Zoology with the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]], becoming a research fellow between 1969 and 1978. He was then promoted to Senior Research Fellow.<ref name=Bio />

== Political career ==
=== Union of Democratic Forces ===
Beron was a founding member and secretary of the SDS (a coalition of multiple opposition groups) when it was formed on 7 December 1989.<ref>[https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/UDF_Coordinating_Council_1990 Coordinating Council of the Union of Democratic Forces.] ''Demokratsiya Newspaper'', 27 April 1990.</ref> He was elected to the 7th [[National Assembly (Bulgaria)#Grand National Assembly|Grand National Assembly]] in the first democratic elections in [[1990 Bulgarian Constitutional Assembly election|1990]].

The SDS leader, [[Zhelyu Zhelev]], was elected president by the Grand National Assembly on August 1, 1990 and so Beron was elected to succeed him as chairman of the party. His tenure was relatively short lived. On December 4 he stepped down after admitting that he had worked as a police informer under the old regime. Beron was one of 70 MPs who were named in secret documents as having spied for the state security. Evidence was uncovered that he was a police informant code-named Bontcho who kept tabs on his colleagues for the secret police.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sudetic |first=Chuck |date=December 4, 1990 |title=Opposition Leader In Bulgaria Quits |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/12/04/world/opposition-leader-in-bulgaria-quits.html |accessdate=27 February 2014 |work=The New York Times |publisher=The New York Times}}</ref> In his defense he insisted that his police activities served the state and not the [[Bulgarian Communist Party|Communist Party]].<ref>{{cite web|last=AP|title=Ex-Opposition Chief In Bulgaria Admits Role as an Informer|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/12/05/world/ex-opposition-chief-in-bulgaria-admits-role-as-an-informer.html|work=New York Times|publisher=The New York Times|accessdate=27 February 2014}}</ref>

He was one of the few people who signed the [[Constitution of Bulgaria]].

Beron left the Union of Democratic Forces is 1991.

=== Vice-Presidential Bid, 1992 ===
In the [[1992 Bulgarian presidential election|January 1992]] presidential elections Beron was the running mate of [[George Ganchev]] - leader of the [[Bulgarian Business Bloc]]. The duo finished third with 853,044 votes (16.8%).

=== Presidential Bid, 2001 ===
Beron ran for president in [[2001 Bulgarian presidential election|2001]] with Stoyan Andreev (from the Bulgarian Union) as his running mate. They finished sixth with only 31,394 votes (1.1%).

=== Back in Parliament 2005-2009 ===
Beron was elected to the [[National Assembly (Bulgaria)|National Assembly]] in the [[2005 Bulgarian parliamentary election|2005]] parliamentary election under the ticket of the new nationalist party - [[Attack (political party)|Attack]]. He split from the party in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nationalist Turns on Ex-Buddy in Bulgaria's Presidential Race|url=http://www.novinite.com/articles/70583/Nationalist+Turns+on+Ex-Buddy+in+Bulgaria%27s+Presidential+Race|work=Novinite.com|publisher=Sofia News Agency|accessdate=27 February 2014}}</ref>

=== Presidential Bid, 2006 ===
Beron ran one last time for president - as an independent this time - in [[2006 Bulgarian presidential election|2006]] with Stela Bankova as his running mate. They finished fifth with only 21,812 votes (0.79%).
